statement.p: Find the maximum and minimum values of the function f(x)=x-\frac{64x}{x+4} on the interval [0,13].

static.solution: f(x) is the solution to f'(x)=0. The derivative isf'(x)=1-\frac{256}{\left(x+4\right)^{2}}. Setting this equal to zero and solving for x gives x=-4\pm 16, and of these two critical points only -4+16=12 lies in our interval. Evaluating f(-4+16)=f(12) yields the critical value -36. The values of the function at the endpoints of the interval are f(0)=0, f(13)=-35.9412, so the minimum value is -36, and the maximum value is 0.
